{{Short description|Way to create new manifolds out of disk bundles}}
[[File:Plumbing_disk_bundles.jpg|thumb|right|alt=Plumbing two 1-disk bundles to get a new 2-manifold.|Plumbing two 1-disk bundles to get a new 2-manifold.]]
In  the mathematical field of [[geometric topology]], among the techniques known as [[surgery theory]], the process of '''plumbing''' is a way to create new [[manifold]]s out of [[sphere bundle|disk bundle]]s. It was first described by [[John Milnor]] (1956) and subsequently used extensively in surgery theory to produce manifolds and [[normal invariant|normal map]]s with given [[surgery obstruction]]s.

== Definition ==

Let <math>\xi_i=(E_i,M_i,p_i)</math> be a [[Rank (linear algebra)|rank]] ''n'' [[vector bundle]] over an ''n''-dimensional [[Differentiable manifold|smooth manifold]] <math>M_i</math> for ''i''&nbsp;=&nbsp;1,2. Denote by <math>D(E_i)</math> the total space of the associated (closed) disk bundle <math>D(\xi_i)</math>and suppose that <math>\xi_i, M_i</math> and <math>D(E_i)</math>are oriented in a compatible way. If we pick two points <math>x_i\in M_i</math>, ''i''&nbsp;=&nbsp;1,2, and consider a ball neighbourhood of <math>x_i</math>  in <math>M_i</math>, then we get neighbourhoods <math>D^n_i\times D^n_i</math> of the fibres over the ball in <math>D(E_i)</math>. Let <math>h:D^n_1\rightarrow D^n_2</math> and <math>k:D^n_1\rightarrow D^n_2</math> be two diffeomorphisms (either both orientation preserving or reversing). The '''plumbing''' (Browder, 1972) of <math>D(E_1)</math> and <math>D(E_2)</math> at <math>x_1</math> and <math>x_2</math> is defined to be the [[Quotient space (topology)|quotient space]] <math>P=D(E_1)\cup_f D(E_2)</math> where <math>f:D^n_1\times D^n_1\rightarrow D^n_2\times D^n_2</math> is defined by <math>f(x,y)=(k(y),h(x))</math>.
The smooth structure on the quotient is  defined by "straightening the angles" (Browder, 1972).

=== Plumbing according to a tree ===
If the base manifold is an ''n''-sphere <math>S^n</math>, then by iterating this procedure over several vector bundles over <math>S^n</math> one can plumb them together according to a [[Tree (graph theory)|tree]] (Hirzebruch et al., 1993, §8). If <math>T</math> is a tree, we assign to each vertex a vector bundle ''<math>\xi</math>'' over <math>S^n</math> and we plumb the corresponding disk bundles together if two vertices are connected by an edge. One has to be careful that neighbourhoods in the total spaces do not overlap.

== Milnor manifolds ==
Let <math>D(\tau_{S^{2k}})</math> denote the disk bundle associated to the [[tangent bundle]] of the ''2k''-sphere. If we plumb eight copies of <math>D(\tau_{S^{2k}})</math> according to the [[Dynkin diagram|diagram <math>E_8</math>]], we obtain a ''4k''-dimensional manifold which certain authors (Madsen and Milgram, 1979; López de Medrano, 1971) call the '''Milnor manifold'''  <math>M^{4k}_B</math> (see also [[E8 manifold|E<sub>8</sub> manifold]]). 

For <math>k>1</math>, the boundary <math>\Sigma^{4k-1}=\partial M^{4k}_B</math> is a [[homotopy sphere]] which generates <math>\theta^{4k-1}(\partial \pi)</math>, the group of [[H-cobordism|''h''-cobordism]] classes of homotopy spheres which bound [[Parallelizable manifold| π-manifolds]] (see also [[exotic sphere|exotic spheres]] for more details). Its signature is <math>sgn(M^{4k}_B)=8</math> and there exists (Browder, 1972, V.2.9) a [[Normal invariant|normal map]]  <math>(f,b)</math> such that the [[surgery obstruction]] is <math>\sigma(f,b)=1</math>, where <math>g:(M^{4k}_B,\partial M^{4k}_B)\rightarrow (D^{4k},S^{4k-1})</math> is a map of degree 1 and <math>b:\nu_{M^{4k}_B} \rightarrow \xi</math> is a [[bundle map]] from the [[stable normal bundle]] of the Milnor manifold to a certain [[stable vector bundle]].

== The plumbing theorem ==

A crucial theorem for the development of surgery theory is the so-called ''Plumbing Theorem'' (Browder, 1972, II.1.3) (presented here in the [[Simply connected space|simply connected]] case):

For all <math>k>1, l\in \Z</math>, there exists a ''2k''-dimensional manifold <math>M</math> with boundary <math>\partial M</math> and a normal map <math>(g,c)</math> where <math>g:(M,\partial M)\rightarrow (D^{2k},S^{2k-1})</math> is such that <math>g|_{\partial M}</math> is a homotopy equivalence, <math>c</math> is a bundle map into the [[Fiber bundle|trivial bundle]] and the surgery obstruction is <math>\sigma(g,c)=l</math>.

The proof of this theorem makes use of the Milnor manifolds defined above.
